newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Anwar says 8.0 pct growth still on cards.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Anwar says 8.0 pct growth still on cards.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Thursday that Malaysia's gross national product (GNP) growth of about 8.0 percent could still be achieved despite sharp weakness in the ringgit.
"We are concerned about macroeconomic stability and we are confident about the fact that fundamentals are in place," Anwar, who is also finance minister, told reporters at a news briefing.
He added, "...in fact we are even able to sustain the growth level of 8.0 to 8.2 pct as projected or estimated earlier."
Asked about the ringgit, Anwar said, "Bank Negara has been entrusted clearly under the provision of the (banking and finance) act to protect (the ringgit)."
"There's of course a level that is acceptable," he said, but declined to specify that level.
"We are concerned, but I think we can manage," he added.
The ringgit pierced the key 2.65 a dollar level earlier on Thursday, but recovered slightly thereafter. At 0911 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.6495/25.
"The minor skirmishes and adjustments required in day-to-day (ringgit) management is certainly not the same as having to ensure a stable macroeconomic management," Anwar said.
